title: the PClassDescriptorConcrete static initialisers, one row per member
heading: ## Per-member rows: the class descriptor each of the PClassDescriptorConcrete static initialisers loads (OPUS, 2026-10-03)
lead: The family `PClassDescriptorConcrete static initialisers` (frontmatter: 254 members; {N} get a row here) shares one shape, stated here once and not repeated per row: each loads its class descriptor X into rcx and calls its own descriptor-constructor wrapper, clears bit 0x2 of dword [X+0xFC], stores the concrete vtable at qword [X], and tail-jumps to 00808B90 with rcx = its static teardown (the atexit registration); all 254 have exactly this nine-instruction form. What differs from member to member is the class descriptor X its `lea rcx, [X]` loads (the first `lea rcx` in the body; the second loads the member's teardown, part of the shared form). Each row anchors the first such `lea`, the member's distinguishing instruction, and states X and the class X describes. The class is read from the certified image: the static initialiser that does `lea rcx, [X]` and calls a descriptor-constructor wrapper, and that wrapper's `lea r8, [name]` before its one call to `00632D80`; every such initialiser must agree. {CHECK} re-derives every row and compares it with the committed {ROWS}. A member whose loads name more than one X, a descriptor not named by exactly one class, or a value that differs fails it. Two controls are refused: a swapped value and a moved anchor. Members that do not derive are listed in [`excluded.tsv`](../../_index/candidates/opus-ee-descriptor-static-initialisers-1003/excluded.tsv).
